tone_reread.name: University of Minnesota-Twin Cities
tone_reread.basis: Mostly procedure; its required statements are framed around dishonesty, copyright and data security, and it ends on a warning.

tone_reread.name: University of Minnesota-Twin Cities
tone_reread.basis: News story on new AI courses and an AI minor; opportunity throughout.

tone_reread.name: Johns Hopkins University
tone_reread.basis: FERPA, HIPAA, copyright and privacy risks make up most of the page.

tone_reread.name: Valparaiso University
tone_reread.basis: The suggested statement warns against 'mindless' use and says AI 'is known to make a lot of mistakes'.

tone_reread.name: Coppin State University
tone_reread.basis: AI appears in university rules only as one item in a list of misconduct, with no evaluative language (codebook v3 rule f). The upbeat AI certificate page is not a rule.

tone_reread.name: Snow College
tone_reread.basis: The purpose section gives AI's 'transformative potential' and a full list of risks (inaccuracy, bias, copyright, privacy) equal weight, and long sections cover prohibited use and cautions.

tone_reread.name: University of Virginia-Main Campus
tone_reread.basis: The faculty guidance encourages appropriate use as an aid to learning, and gives as much space to cheating, privacy, intellectual property and the limits of AI grading and detection.

tone_reread.name: Massachusetts Institute of Technology
tone_reread.basis: Procedural memo about class AI policies; no evaluative language.

tone_reread.name: Luzerne County Community College
tone_reread.basis: AI appears only as items in the list of violations, with no evaluative language (codebook v3 rule f).

tone_reread.name: University of Cincinnati
tone_reread.basis: 'AI is a powerful partner'; the page says it is 'not intended as a list of restrictions'; its data cautions are practical.

tone_reread.name: The Ohio State University
tone_reread.basis: The AI Fluency initiative; opportunity throughout.

tone_reread.name: Defiance College
tone_reread.basis: The only AI text found is the Pilgrim Library's AI guide, in the library's own words, so under codebook v3 rule (c) it does not count. The catalog's Academic Integrity Policy and the Student Handbook do not mention AI.

tone_reread.name: Columbus State Community College
tone_reread.basis: Standard syllabus statement: a default rule with one balanced sentence.

tone_reread.name: Iowa State University
tone_reread.basis: The conduct office warns that AI use 'regularly results' in misconduct findings: a warning, not only a list item.

tone_reread.name: Stanford University
tone_reread.basis: A default course policy, mostly procedural, with one balanced framing sentence.

tone_reread.name: New York Institute of Technology
tone_reread.basis: The policy's AI text is a list of unauthorized uses followed by sanctions, with no evaluative language (codebook v3 rule f). The November 2025 student guide is more upbeat, but the policy is the page coded.

tone_reread.name: West Virginia Wesleyan College
tone_reread.basis: A long procedural policy (definitions, data security, integrity) with brief balanced framing.

tone_reread.name: Glendale Community College
tone_reread.basis: AI appears only in the misconduct definitions, followed by the regulation's standard consequences, with no evaluative language (codebook v3 rule f).

tone_reread.name: Arizona State University Campus Immersion
tone_reread.basis: 'Principled innovation', tools offered to faculty, 'the positive potential of generative AI'.

tone_reread.name: Arizona State University Campus Immersion
tone_reread.basis: One handbook rule that calls unallowed AI use academic dishonesty, followed by its sanction, with no evaluative language (codebook v3 rule f).

tone_reread.name: Rice University
tone_reread.basis: Honor Council page on accusations and detectors; it tells professors to 'highlight the downsides of using AI'.

tone_reread.name: Rice University
tone_reread.basis: News story on two new AI courses; opportunity throughout.

tone_reread.name: Eastern Kentucky University
tone_reread.basis: One sentence on efficiency, then data privacy and security risks fill the page.

tone_reread.name: Nevada State University
tone_reread.basis: Every classroom use in the page's table comes with pitfalls ('catastrophic outcomes', 'bland and trite'), next to calling AI 'a very effective tool' and 'a great way' to start.

tone_reread.name: Nevada State University
tone_reread.basis: One procedural line pointing students to each syllabus.

tone_reread.name: University of the District of Columbia
tone_reread.basis: The president's AI Initiative; opportunity throughout, with human oversight as a principle.

tone_reread.name: University of Missouri-Kansas City
tone_reread.basis: The Provost encourages teaching ethical use 'rather than banning'; the detector warning is about detectors, not AI.

tone_reread.name: University of Pennsylvania
tone_reread.basis: Mostly instructions for writing course policies; its few evaluative lines are balanced but brief.

tone_reread.name: College of Charleston
tone_reread.basis: 'Transformative potential', tutor and creative partner; limits are named but opportunity leads.

tone_reread.name: Westminster College
tone_reread.basis: AI appears only as an item in procedural lists of violations (codebook v3 rule f).

tone_reread.name: Niagara County Community College
tone_reread.basis: Procedural rules on integrity, data privacy and tool approval.

tone_reread.name: Temple University
tone_reread.basis: The policy's stated goal weighs exploring AI against protecting chances to learn; the page says the value of a tool 'depends on your purpose'.

tone_reread.name: Nova Southeastern University
tone_reread.basis: The page calls generative AI 'transforming' and a faculty partner and lists research advantages, and gives a long section to cheating, detector false positives and output pitfalls.

tone_reread.name: University of Maine at Fort Kent
tone_reread.basis: The official guidance aims 'to promote innovation while ensuring integrity': AI tools are 'wonderful' and 'transformative' but 'should never replace' critical thinking, with privacy cautions.

tone_reread.name: Berry College
tone_reread.basis: Official syllabus statement; procedural (see the re-sourced value).

tone_reread.name: Tidewater Community College
tone_reread.basis: See the re-sourced value.

tone_reread.name: Case Western Reserve University
tone_reread.basis: 'Embraces AI in education to prepare students for the workforce'; the sample statements range from a ban to open use.
